body: Luka Dončić keeps finding new gears. He scored a season-high 53 points, with five rebounds and five assists, as the Los Angeles Lakers came back to beat the Portland Trail Blazers 124-118 in NBA Cup play on Nov. 6.
It was his seventh straight game with at least 35 points, five rebounds and five assists, which ties Oscar Robertson for the longest such run in NBA history, according to NBA.com.
## Why fans are buying in

When we wrote about Dončić on Nov. 4, the story was a five-game scoring run. Since then it has turned into something historic. This was his fourth straight 40-point game, a stretch only Kobe Bryant, Elgin Baylor and George Mikan had reached for the Lakers before him, per ESPN. He is averaging 40.1 points a game, and only Wilt Chamberlain has scored more points through the first nine games of a season.

He also carried the comeback. Los Angeles trailed by seven at halftime, Dončić hit a shot from beyond half court at the buzzer, and then scored 20 points in a third quarter the Lakers won 34-15. It was the 11th 50-point game of his career and his fourth as a Laker.

The win lifted the Lakers to 8-2 and into first place in the Western Conference. Dončić already ranked No. 2 on the NBA's list of top-selling jerseys for the 2025-26 regular season, based on online sales through the NBA Store and the Fanatics network. In our analysis, a run that has fans comparing him to Robertson and Chamberlain only adds to that pull. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Jayson Tatum looked like his old self in Charlotte. He scored 34 points on 9-of-16 shooting, with nine assists, eight rebounds and five 3-pointers, as the Boston Celtics beat the Hornets 119-80 on Nov. 6. He did it in three quarters.
Eighteen of those points came in the first quarter, and Boston never looked back.
## Why fans are buying in

This is Tatum's first full season since he ruptured his Achilles tendon in the 2025 playoffs. He did not return until March 6, 2026, and played 16 regular-season games before Boston's first-round exit. A night like this one is the clearest sign yet that he is all the way back.
It also came after a cold start from deep. He had been shooting 22% from 3-point range before Friday, according to Boston.com, then made five. As a team, Boston hit 24 of 44 from deep.

The Celtics are winning around him. They are 7-2, have won seven of their last eight, and sit first in their NBA Cup group at 2-0. With Jaylen Brown now playing in Philadelphia, this is more clearly Tatum's team than ever.

Fans never stopped backing him. Even in a season with only 16 games, Tatum ranked No. 7 on the NBA's list of top-selling jerseys for the 2025-26 regular season, based on online sales through the NBA Store and the Fanatics network. In our analysis, a healthy Tatum leading a winning team gives that support a new reason to grow. This is our view, not a sales figure.

body: Kirill Kaprizov is the most dangerous scorer in hockey right now. He had a goal and three assists as the Minnesota Wild beat the San Jose Sharks 4-1 at home on Nov. 6, and his 16 goals lead the NHL.

He opened the scoring on a two-man advantage, one-timing a cross-ice feed from Quinn Hughes, and then set up a Maxim Shabanov power-play goal in the second period. Jesper Wallstedt handled the rest with 23 saves.
## Why fans are buying in

Kaprizov has points in seven straight games, with five goals and eight assists in that stretch. Minnesota is 12-3-3, has won three in a row and is 6-0-1 in its last seven. The Wild are 10-1-1 when he scores, according to NHL.com.

The same night, the Wild became the fastest franchise in NHL history to reach 1,000 regular-season wins. Kaprizov has been the face of that history for years. He won the Calder Trophy in 2021, set the team's single-season records for goals and points in 2021-22, and broke Zach Parise's franchise record for playoff goals last spring. Before he reached the NHL, he scored the overtime goal that won Olympic gold in 2018.
Minnesota has bet on him for the long haul. He signed an eight-year, $136 million extension on Sept. 30, 2025, worth $17 million a year, and it began this season.
In our analysis, the NHL's goal leader on a winning team, locked in for years, is the kind of player whose jersey keeps gaining fans. This is our view, not a sales figure.
